id.description: The unique identifier for the chat

name.description: The name of the chat (for group chats)

type.description: The type of chat (direct message or group chat)

participantIds.description: Array of user IDs participating in the chat

lastMessageId.description: ID of the most recent message in the chat

updatedAt.description: When the chat was last updated

admins.description: Administrators of a group chat, as eNames ("@<uuid>"). Older writers store User profile ids here instead; resolve them the way evault-core does. This is a SEED for the group's manifest: evault-core reads it once, when it builds the manifest of a group vault that has none (ManifestService, on the first /whois of that vault), and from then on the manifest is authoritative and changes here are not read. A platform changing admins of a group that has a manifest writes the manifest. It is read directly only for a group chat whose document does not live on a group vault of its own. Some writers use `adminIds` for the same thing; it is not part of this schema.

rights.description: What members of this chat may do. A policy the platform showing the chat is expected to honour; the vault does not enforce it. An ABSENT `rights`, or an ABSENT key inside it, means the platform's built-in default (members may do it); an EMPTY `allow` means nobody but the owner and admins. The owner (from the group manifest) and the admins hold every right, and a `deny` naming them is ignored. Not used in direct chats: two equal members have nobody to set it. `rights` is always written as a whole: an eVault update replaces a top-level field, so concurrent writers race and the last one wins; `revision` lets a later reader NOTICE a lost change, it does not prevent one. Writers that do not know `rights` leave it untouched.

react.description: React to and comment on a live broadcast in the chat.

watch.description: See a live broadcast in the chat.

join.description: Take part in calls in the chat: be rung, see that a call is running, join it. Being in a call does not mean speaking; without this right a member is never rung and cannot join, and may only watch a live broadcast if they have `watch`.

show.description: Publish camera and screen in a call.

call.description: Start a call in the chat.

revision.description: Increased by one on every change. A writer re-reads the chat first and writes its revision + 1; a lower revision seen later means another writer replaced `rights` from an older copy.

updatedBy.description: eName of whoever made the last change.

updatedAt.description: When the last change was made.

allow.description: eNames allowed, or "*" for every participant of the chat at the time of the check, including those who join later. Empty means nobody (besides owner and admins).

deny.description: eNames refused. Deny wins over allow. "*" is not allowed: 'nobody' is an empty allow.
